findings.issue: GET search uses search_index -> index_connection, which opens a writable connection and can DROP legacy videos/vectors tables. Web search must use a read-only connection without automatic schema migration.
Interpolating an unescaped filesystem path into the SQLite URI lets a # in --root swallow mode=ro and can open/create a different writable file.
Non-loopback --host only warns and exposes the unauthenticated library. A caller can supply a loopback Host header remotely; the issue excludes unauthenticated remote service.
IPv6 loopback is allowlisted but Host parsing rejects [::1]:port, and serve uses an IPv4 server that cannot bind ::1.
Foreign Origin requests with a valid local Host reach routes, contrary to W0's required Origin policy.
Missing or incompatible indexes produce a generic 500 instead of safe maintenance states such as the W0-required migration_required; reads must leave legacy data untouched.
W0 requires a health check, but no health route exists.
KeyboardInterrupt escapes serve_forever without closing the server socket, so W0 graceful shutdown is incomplete.
A malformed absolute request target such as http://[ raises ValueError outside the error boundary and drops the connection without an HTTP response.
HTML escaping does not URL-encode indexed job IDs, and the detail route does not URL-decode them; IDs containing spaces, Unicode, #, ? or % cannot round-trip.
HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE and CONNECT fall through to stdlib 501 responses without the configured security headers, contradicting the claimed non-GET 405 behavior.

summary: Fixed 11 W0 defects, including destructive GET search migrations, unescaped SQLite URIs, unauthenticated remote binds, and missing security/lifecycle handling. Git Bash validation passes 27 tests plus the CLI self-test; the full suite still has eight pre-existing Windows operations.db cleanup failures reproduced on unchanged main. All fixes are local; nothing was pushed.
